text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap).
The history of a red, scaly rash appearing in a 3-month-old, exacerbated by cold weather, combined with a family history of psoriasis, is highly characteristic of this condition. The father's history of psoriasis may suggest a genetic predisposition to skin barrier issues or psoriasis itself, but the clinical presentation of "seborrheic" dermatitis in an infant is the primary working diagnosis.
